title: Modern Management
paragraphs: After inheriting a department with notoriously low morale and inefficient processes, Yasmin decided against implementing the sweeping structural changes her predecessor's replacement had originally recommended during the transition period.

Instead, she spent her first month conducting individual conversations with every team member, an approach some senior colleagues considered an inefficient use of a new manager's limited time and organizational credibility.

These conversations revealed that most persistent problems stemmed not from structural inefficiency but from a specific, previously unaddressed process that consistently created unnecessary friction between two closely related teams.

Rather than redesigning the entire department as originally suggested, Yasmin implemented a single, targeted fix addressing this specific friction point, a modest intervention that nonetheless produced substantial improvement in overall team functioning.

Team members frequently commented that being genuinely heard, rather than simply having new processes imposed upon them without consultation, significantly improved their engagement independent of the specific structural changes themselves.

Reflecting on this experience, Yasmin concluded that effective modern management often requires resisting the temptation toward comprehensive restructuring in favor of precisely targeted interventions informed by genuine understanding of underlying, specific problems.
